record.title: Evidence-gated authority in language-model review trades fewer corruptions of correct proposals for missed welfare-only repairs
record.summary: In a September 2026 paper, Fuad Ali compares broad reviewer override with a rule that lets a reviewer replace an upstream proposal only after it supplies a mechanically valid certificate of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. The paper reports paired experiments with Qwen3-8B and Mistral-Small-24B on 96 synthetic spatial-policy tasks and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark. The gate prevents changes to correct proposals by construction, but also bars welfare improvements to compliant, suboptimal proposals. A prospective retain/replace/escalate interface protects correct proposals for Qwen, which then declines welfare-only repairs; Mistral still replaces and corrupts all 48 correct proposals in that test. These are author-reported results from quantized local models and structured synthetic tasks, not evidence of deployment prevalence or a model-independent safety guarantee.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper compares broad reviewer override with evidence-gated authority that permits replacement only after a mechanically checked binding-constraint violation and compliant repair.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 96 synthetic spatial-policy tasks, the paper reports that broad review changed 85 of 96 correct proposals to non-optimal alternatives for each model; the evidence gate retained all correct proposals and gave an 88.5 percentage-point exact-optimality effect in that condition, while forgoing some repairs to compliant but suboptimal proposals.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the paper reports that the evidence gate protected correct proposals but substantially reduced exact-welfare repairs of compliant suboptimal proposals; the reported magnitudes differed between Qwen3-8B and Mistral-Small-24B.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a prospective retain/replace/escalate interface test on 48 tasks per proposal state, Qwen retained all 48 correct and all 48 compliant-suboptimal proposals, while Mistral replaced and corrupted all 48 correct proposals; therefore the interface was not a model-independent safeguard in this test.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish real-world deployment prevalence, performance with frontier APIs or human reviewers, or that evidence-gated review is universally safer or welfare-optimal.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent recomputation or reproduction of the reported task outcomes and confidence intervals was performed in this activation.
The experiments do not measure deployment prevalence of correct, violating and compliant-suboptimal upstream proposals.
The study does not establish effects with frontier APIs, human reviewers, open-ended actions or contested constraints.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported mechanism transfers to deployed agent review, restricting binding authority to mechanically evidenced violations could reduce corruption of already-correct actions, while also suppressing valid optimization repairs. Consequence depends on upstream state prevalence, reviewer behavior and domain transfer; the evidence is two-model synthetic-task research, not deployment safety or prevalence.
limitations: All numeric outcomes are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced in this record.
Only two quantized open-weight models were tested; results do not establish behavior for frontier APIs, human reviewers or heterogeneous teams.
Tasks use structured seven-option synthetic tables with mechanically known objectives; transfer to open-ended or contested real decisions is not established.
Natural proposal-state frequencies come from one prompt family and benchmark, not deployment prevalence.
The action-menu test changes the prompt and reviewer output; it does not isolate authorization while holding reviewer behavior fixed.
brief.summary: In a September 2026 paper, Fuad Ali compares broad reviewer override with a rule that lets a reviewer replace an upstream proposal only after it supplies a mechanically valid certificate of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. The paper reports paired experiments with Qwen3-8B and Mistral-Small-24B on 96 synthetic spatial-policy tasks and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark. The gate prevents changes to correct proposals by construction, but also bars welfare improvements to compliant, suboptimal proposals. A prospective retain/replace/escalate interface protects correct proposals for Qwen, which then declines welfare-only repairs; Mistral still replaces and corrupts all 48 correct proposals in that test. These are author-reported results from quantized local models and structured synthetic tasks, not evidence of deployment prevalence or a model-independent safety guarantee.

technical.claimed_result: Across two locally run quantized open-weight models, 96 spatial-policy tasks and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the paper reports a correction–corruption tradeoff. Gating protected correct proposals but barred repairs of compliant suboptimal proposals. An explicit action menu protected correct proposals for Qwen while failing to do so for Mistral.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper says the frozen results can be audited and manuscript artifacts rebuilt without paid API calls; no costs were independently measured in this review.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper establishes that its authors published this design, benchmark methods and results. This review directly inspected the full arXiv HTML and submission date; it did not independently reproduce the experiments or rebuild the frozen artifacts.
technical.mechanism: A reviewer can bind a recommended replacement either whenever its structured response parses (broad override) or only when a deterministic checker verifies a binding-constraint violation and compliant repair (evidence gate). The paired comparison holds the reviewer output fixed; a separate action-menu experiment changes reviewer behavior and is not an authorization-only comparison.
technical.regime: Two quantized locally run models (Qwen3-8B and Mistral-Small-24B), seven-option structured tasks, synthetic spatial-policy and public-project portfolio domains, temperature-zero generation and mechanically available task ground truth.
technical.reproducibility: The arXiv record links an MIT-licensed repository that describes frozen processed results, raw model request/response outputs and deterministic table/figure rebuild instructions. This activation did not pin the repository commit, retrieve the frozen archive or rebuild artifacts; independent reproduction remains open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Paired broad-override condition with the same fixed reviewer output is the primary comparator. The action-menu comparison changes the prompt and response and is interpreted separately.

brief.title: Evidence-gated authority in language-model review trades fewer corruptions of correct proposals for missed welfare-only repairs
brief.why_it_matters: The study makes reviewer authority a measurable system design choice: the same review output can repair violations or corrupt correct actions depending on which changes are allowed to bind. Its reported results expose a correction–corruption tradeoff that depends on model behavior, interface and upstream proposal states. The paper does not establish which rule is best in deployed systems; evidence-gate checks, task distributions and human escalation require separate evaluation.
